Issued at 300 PM EDT Fri Sep 25 2026

Through Tonight...A mid-level cutoff low paired with a developing
nor'easter just off the coast of the Carolinas at the surface 
continues to slowly drift northward, with the attendant cold front
draped across the Atlantic and angled across south Florida, where
it has also slowly drifted southward today. Locally, breezy 
northeast winds persist behind the front around 15 to 20 mph with 
gusts up to 30 mph possible at times, highest along the coast. 
Isolated to scattered shower development also continues across the
local Atlantic waters. A few light, isolated showers have managed
to develop and push onshore along the immediate coast today and 
this activity is expected to continue over the next few hours with
the greatest rain chances (20%) focused along the coast south of 
the Cape. Elsewhere, conditions across east central Florida have 
remained mostly dry today as a drier air mass settles across the 
area. The GOES19 Total PWAT viewer shows PWAT values as low as 
1.1" in some spots north of the I-4 corridor. This drier air will 
continue to settle across the area through the evening and 
overnight hours, with mostly dry conditions forecast through 
tonight as the northerly winds slacken to around 10 mph. There 
remains a low chance (20%) of shower activity along the Treasure 
Coast overnight. Temperatures remain on track to peak in the low 
to mid 80s this afternoon, falling into the 60s tonight. The 
coolest overnight temperatures will be focused near and north of 
the I-4 corridor, remaining in the upper 60s along the coast. 

Hazardous beach conditions continue along the east central 
Florida coast. Breaking waves of 4 to 9 feet and a high risk of 
rip currents will continue through the remainder of today and into
the overnight hours. A High Surf Advisory continues through at 
least 4 AM Sunday. While entering the ocean already is not advised
at night, with these surf conditions, entering the ocean is 
strongly discouraged.

Saturday-Monday...While the nor'easter continues northward into 
the Mid Atlantic and New England area this weekend and into early 
next week, broad surface high pressure is anticipated to slowly 
build across the Florida peninsula as drier air settles locally. 
PWATs are forecast to fall into the 1-1.2" range areawide, with 
little to no rain and storm chances anticipated through this 
weekend and into next week. Some lingering breezy northerly winds 
will persist into Saturday, highest along the coast, before 
diminishing and becoming light and variable Sunday and Monday. 
Temperatures are anticipated to remain seasonable through the 
weekend, ranging between the low to mid 80s each afternoon, 
warming slightly into the mid to upper 80s on Monday. Lows in the 
60s persist.

While the weather will be pleasant through this weekend, 
conditions at the beaches are anticipated to remain poor to 
hazardous. Persistent breezy and gusty northeast winds the last 
couple of days have resulted in building seas that will be slow to
subside through the weekend and into early next week. A high risk
of rip currents is anticipated through at least Saturday, though 
it will likely continue into Sunday as well. Breaking waves of 3 
to 6 feet will also persist, so rough, hazardous surf will also be
present. Overall, entering the ocean is strongly discouraged this
weekend.

Tuesday-Thursday...While the mid-level cutoff low near the Mid 
Atlantic and northeastern US continues lifting northward and 
weakens, another mid-level trough is forecast to move towards the 
southeast US and the Florida peninsula. The trough is expected to 
drift southward, reaching the eastern Gulf mid to late week. At 
the surface, broad high pressure across the Atlantic is 
anticipated to lift northward, with guidance hinting at some sort 
of disturbance developing in the Gulf and lifting northwestward, 
potentially resulting in a boundary lifting northward across the 
Florida peninsula. This set-up would result in increasing moisture
locally, aided by initially southeast winds on Tuesday that 
become more onshore Wednesday onward. A return of rain and storm 
chances to east central Florida is forecast, with PoPs near to 
slightly above normal. While it is too early to pin down exact 
storm threats, the typical lightning, gusty winds, and heavy 
downpours all look to be reasonable hazards with activity. It is 
important to note that there remains some discrepancies between 
guidance, so shifts and adjustments to rain and storm chances are 
likely as models come into better agreement and the timing becomes
clearer. The increasing moisture will result in slightly warmer 
temperatures, with highs and lows near to slightly above normal
